children: Investors are rewarding Jersey Mike's for getting people to buy more of its subs at a time when many restaurants are struggling to increase transactions.
The New Jersey-based sandwich chain's shares were up 7% Wednesday after it released its first earnings report as a public company.

Same-store sales grew 2.3% in the three months ended June 28 from a year earlier, driven by transaction growth for sandwich options like chicken salad. Jersey Mike's said it expects same-store sales to grow more swiftly in its third quarter and be up at least 2.5% for the full year.
The company said it expects to continue to attract new customers through revamped marketing and a handful of limited-time offers a year.
